recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the FHIR-41688 reconciliation without broadening the issue into separate resource-specific search parameter work; handle Group-specific or additional Range search parameters under their own Jira issues such as FHIR-40341.
issue_request: FHIR-41688 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 by FHIR-I. It asked for search behavior on Range-typed data to be defined, with final guidance to use composite search parameters rather than adding a new range search type, modifier, or delimiter.
initial_application: The combined branch already contained source commit 10af8c0a5aff3957b36d6c901af64f0d577e1877, which added Range/composite guidance to source/search.html but lacked an Issue-Reconcile-Key trailer. That application documented object-level joining for repeated references to the same underlying Range search parameter, but the POST body in the new example used value-range-values=le20$ge30 while the GET form and prose used ge20$le30.
additional_context: The linked Zulip implementers thread starts from a Group.characteristic valueRange use case and records implementer feedback that composites are the least disruptive option. FHIR-I minutes on 2025-03-24 record a 13-0-0 motion that FHIR-41688 can be handled with composite parameters and that no new search parameter type is desired. A later FHIR-40341 discussion is related Group-specific Range/quantity search work and was kept out of this seed decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/search.html so the POST form of the Range composite example uses value-range-values=ge20$le30, matching the GET query and the statement that the same Range instance must have low >= 20 and high <= 30.
source_changes: source/search.html: corrected the POST body in the Searching ranges composite example from value-range-values=le20$ge30 to value-range-values=ge20$le30.

related_jiras.note: Adjacent Applied R6 issue about Group characteristic valueQuantity/valueRange and exclude search parameters; relevant background but not decided here because it requires a separate Group-specific reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: Applied/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I issue requesting defined Range search behavior, resolved as composite search parameter guidance rather than a new search type or modifier.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the approved seed behavior: same-underlying Range components in a composite must join at the object level and examples should show explicit Range boundary searches.

evidence_items.summary: The linked thread starts from a Group.characteristic valueRange use case and discusses repeated-value range false positives and composite search parameters as the least disruptive path.
evidence_items.learned: The community discussion supports the Jira resolution to document composite Range searches instead of inventing a new generic Range search syntax.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-I minutes record that FHIR-41688 can be handled with composite parameters today and that Zulip showed no interest in a new search parameter type; motion passed 13-0-0.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms the formal WG decision behind the Applied Jira status and narrows the fix to composite guidance/examples.

evidence_items.summary: The current search page documents explicit boundary searching on Range using composites, same-Range-instance joining, and the value-range-values example.
evidence_items.learned: This is the authoritative source location for the seed; after reconciliation the GET and POST forms both use value-range-values=ge20$le30 consistently with the prose.
